At the beginning of the game, each player gets a set of citizen cards, a tribe board, as well as a player board. The tribe board shows your unique tribe ability and the ancient technologies that you may relearn during the game. The player board is where you place your custom machines and upgrade your card slots. A main goal of the game is to reach and populate the large ancient sites. These ancient locations are randomized, and as they are important sources of victory points, they will shape your strategy differently each game. The game ends when all artifacts have been taken, and the player with the most points wins. Number of players: 2 - 4 Game duration: 54 mn Complexity: 4 / 5 Play Revive and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Important notes 2 About the Game 3 Turn overview 4 Play a card 5 Use your Switch 6 Explore 7 Build 8 Populate 9 Hibernate 10 Paying for range 11 Machines and the machine track 12 Tribe abilities 13 Points 14 Artifacts and Artifact cards 15 End of the game 16 Expansion Rules 16.1 Devotion Points 16.2 Scyphoz Cards 16.3 Journey Cards 16.4 Lakes Important notes If you already know the game, here are a few things you should know about this implementation: The crystal conversion is automated. Whenever you need to pay more than you have of a resource, the game will just use your crystals. If you get a surplus of crystals you can convert them. Each turn is strictly split into 2 parts for the 2 actions(unless the player hibernates). Every free action you do is considered part of the respective main action. It has already been clarified on BGG, that you can use crates for payment even if the crate would otherwise push you beyond the resource-limit. Here you can temporarily get beyond the limit within the action. At the end of that action any surplus is lost. If you want to do a free action before your second action that would give you a surplus for that action, you need to finish the first action with the button 'next action' first. When playing with the expansion, every point and devotion point you gain during an action, can be summed up to be converted 2:1 The machine, that allows you to treat a card as any color for 1 action can only be used for card that is being played. If you play on a small screen, the supply/market is not visible per default. You can open with a button inthe action bar. If you're missing the player aid, go to user settings and turn on the help button, it will provide something similar About the Game In Revive, you explore the land, so that you can populate and build on it. Each player has a tribe with a special ability and technologies that can be unlocked by populating. They also have 3 machine tracks. Advancing on them can unlock free actions(machines) and other bonuses. There are 3 basic Resources (gear, book, and food) and crystals which can be converted into any of the 3. The resources you can have are limited (max 3 crystals and 6 of each of the others). But when you get more crystals you can just convert them to any other. Turn overview During your turn may either A) Take 2 Main Actions (different or the same): • Play a card • Use your Switch • Explore • Build • Populate or B) Hibernate At any point during your turn (before between or after your 2 Actions, even before, during or after hibernating) you may • use a machine • use a crate • use a special trade action that you unlocked with one of your technologies The Main Actions in detail: Play a card At the start of the game (after the setup is complete) you have 6 citizen cards. 3 of them are in your active area visible for all. The other 3 form your rest area (facedown but accessible for all) on the right of your player board. Each card has 2 parts: One at the top and one at the bottom. [Rating: 1/10] Another modern solitaire euro. Not for me. At least I did give it a try and wasted another 2 hours of my life for this trash, what some people call a "game"

[Rating: 1/10] For a modern Euro engine builder/resource converter/point salad this design is better than most. Many worse and/or longer games out there such as Ark Nova/Boonlake/Mosaic etc. After learning it is probably  2 hours for 3p.  4p could be painful and if you have players with AP the game could drag. But at the end of the day this is just another themeless head down exercise in puzzle maths. [Rating: 2/10] Do you love playing board games where it doesn't matter what others do? Here you go, a multiplayer solitaire game. You have dozens of possibilities which lead to AP for some players. And because you don't care what others do, you just sit there and wait for your turn. You have no control if others play correctly because it's too fiddly, here a resource there a resource, multiple tracks, multiple bonus stuff and so on.  100% abstract, the theme is not here. [Rating: 2/10] Euro-"slop". And I meant more in the sense how it muddles your memory. Couldn't remember that I've played this, but apparrently I have. Actually rather impressive, if you think about it, how Eurogamers are able to differentiate and compare these things. Much-needed skill in this hobby.

[Rating: 2/10] this comment is based on the fact that I bought this to play solo.  it's false advertising to claim to have a solo mode when there really isn't one.  a solo mode is designed as such and has an AI.  this game's solo mode is "play by yourself and score as many points as you can in X rounds".  I can do that with pretty much any board game--it's not a solo mode.  it's 2025.  game designers should know this (and DO know this), so it's kind of a BS move to claim this is a solo mode for your game when this is all you provide.

[Rating: 2.7/10] + hochwertige Qualität - Tisch zu klein - Maschine unthematisch und unübersichtlich - enorme downtime - Design und Thema

[Rating: 3/10] A very typical modern euro with tracks to move along, resources to gather and convert, engines to build, many levers to pull, last ounces of optimisation to be wrung out, and point salad scoring.  Throw in significant downtime if you have an opponent even remotely prone to analysis paralysis and a very low level of player interaction.  Had the designers added a roll and write element, they would have had the full bingo card of things I dislike in games.  The artwork is quite distinctive and attractive.  Production quality is to a good standard.
